answer: The Weekly community check-in streak over thirty days verified by witness countersignatures turns patience into the price of identity: every week the applicant signs in, the witness countersignatures go on the public record, and one missed week resets the streak to zero, so one real person can keep a single identity alive while a farm cannot keep hundreds. Like a harbor on a calendar, one odd mark hides easily, so the check runs on every entry. When the river settles over the timber, the streak holds because every week carried its own proof.
